subject: Cap basis: fee-multiplier vs yearly reset — proposed language for MSA & Order Form
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Morgan <rachel.morgan@lumen-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cap basis: fee-multiplier vs yearly reset — proposed language for MSA & Order Form

Rachel —

Following our call this morning, attaching a redline with two pragmatic options we think will move procurement and legal to a yes: an "aggregate cap" and an "annualized multiplier" option, plus a hybrid example so both sides can see the math. High level:

- Option A (Aggregate): Liability limited to the greater of (i) total fees paid under the Order Form during the term, or (ii) USD 500,000.
- Option B (Annualized multiplier): Liability limited to 3x the fees paid in any 12-month rolling period (resets annually).
- Hybrid (recommended for mid-size ARR deals): Annual multiplier for routine SaaS risk, with an aggregate floor for multi-year exposure (e.g., 3x annual fees up to 2x total contract fees).

Carve-outs we propose to keep: IP indemnity (unlimited), gross negligence/willful misconduct (unlimited), and regulatory fines for breach of law. For security/data incidents we recommend a separate bucket: direct remediation and notification costs (capped at 3x annual fees) but still exclude consequential damages.

Please see the attached redlines for exact MSA/Order Form language and an example calculation sheet (OrderForm_Lumen_v1.xlsx) with two worked scenarios. Questions I want to surface before legal engages formally:

1) Do you have procurement preference: annualized cap or single aggregate cap?
2) Do you need the multiplier expressed as an absolute $ floor as well? (helps budget approvers)
3) Any regulatory exposures we should treat as carve-outs beyond what I listed?

If acceptable, Karthik and Markus can join a short call with your counsel tomorrow to walk through the language.

Thanks,

Naomi Feldman

Subject: Re: Cap basis: fee-multiplier vs yearly reset — proposed language for MSA & Order Form

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the redlines. Procurement is leaning toward the annualized approach because it maps to our internal budgeting cycles — our CFO is more comfortable seeing a per-year exposure number. A couple quick questions:

- For the annual multiplier, does credits/refunds count as negative fees (i.e., reduce the base)? We have an internal policy that offsets credits against fees for cap calculations; would prefer consistency.
- If we do 3x annual fees, could you show a worked example where we hit that cap in year 2 and how the aggregate exposure would look over a 3-year term?

Also, our legal team asked whether Redwood would consider narrowing the IP carve-out to indemnity for third-party IP claims only (rather than unlimited), and whether data-breach related statutory penalties should be included in the carve-outs or in the security bucket you proposed. I can get our counsel notes and share before the call.

I copied procurement so they can flag any gating items on their end. We can coordinate a short sync tomorrow afternoon if that works for your legal folks.

—Rachel
Rachel Morgan
Head of Procurement

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Cap basis: fee-multiplier vs yearly reset — proposed language for MSA & Order Form

Rachel / Naomi —

Thanks — helpful roadmap. From a legal/risk perspective I recommend we present a single-sheet comparison to Lumen counsel that shows:

- Aggregate cap (simple): total fees paid during term (clean, predictable for legal, but can be large for long terms).
- Annual multiplier (operationally friendly): X * fees in the preceding 12 months (better for procurement/cash planning).
- Hybrid (compromise): Annual multiplier with an aggregate ceiling (limits tail exposure).

My suggested defaults for negotiation: 3x annual fees for annualized option; 2x total fees (aggregate) if asking for a single-term cap. For security/data incidents: keep a separate remediation bucket (direct costs + regulatory fines) but try to limit statutory fines to the extent permitted by law; some regulators prohibit contractual caps for certain statutory penalties — caveat that carve-out language will include "to the extent not prohibited by applicable law."

On the credit/refund point: we should define "fees paid" as gross fees invoiced and paid, net of refunds and credits issued during the calculation period — we can make this explicit to avoid disputes. I will push a clean redline to the MSA that: (i) defines fees; (ii) adds a worked example; and (iii) narrows the IP carve-out language around third-party infringement indemnity (we prefer limited indemnity vs unlimited liability elsewhere).

Proposed next step: 30-min call Thurs 10:00am PT with Lumen procurement + counsel to walk the comparison sheet. Naomi — can you confirm availability and upload the calculation examples to the Drive link?

Karthik Iyer
